- When sentiment turns negative in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price momentum; model tends to overreact to negative sentiment.  
- If recent history shows a sharp upward spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often over-forecasts continuation; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 0.00 or 1.00 alternating), model tends to overestimate mean reversion; adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 days, suggest a “lag correction” — add 1–3% to forecast for each day of lagged underperformance.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >5% avg. daily gain), model often underestimates; apply a “trend amplification” rule: add 1–2% to forecast for each 1% above 5% avg. gain.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple -1.00 entries, model tends to underreact; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for sentiment-induced underestimation.
